title: Get workshop-ready: your AI agent on your laptop · hancrafted
description: A step-by-step guide for first-timers on Mac, Windows or Linux: open your terminal, install and sign in to your AI agent, start it in the starter folder and run your first skill, so the workshop can begin right away.

Overview Say how many steps The W3C advises saying on the first step how many steps follow and on each step how far along the user is, for example "Step 2 of 4" 1 . Sources (1) W3C Web Accessibility Initiative, Forms Tutorial: Multi-page Forms ( opens in a new tab ) w3.org A head start finishes more Car-wash loyalty cards with two pre-stamped stamps out of ten were redeemed by 34% of customers, against 19% for blank cards; the transfer from loyalty cards to a setup guide is an inference 1 . Sources (1) Nunes and Drèze, The Endowed Progress Effect: How Artificial Advancement Increases Effort ( opens in a new tab ) doi.org Minimal still needs a way out A minimal manual, centred on real tasks, taught faster than a standard manual in a study of 64 students, but beginners still need error-recovery material, which is why every step has a troubleshooting box 1 2 . Sources (2) Lazonder and van der Meij, The minimal manual: is less really more? ( opens in a new tab ) doi.org Kalyuga, Ayres, Chandler and Sweller, The Expertise Reversal Effect ( opens in a new tab ) doi.org

Open your terminal Hesitation is normal Computer anxiety is a long-studied, widespread reaction; about 80% of the 89 studies on experience found more experience went with less anxiety, and a relaxed first experience was linked to lower anxiety. No study measures fear of the terminal itself, so applying this to the terminal is an inference 1 . Sources (1) Powell, Computer anxiety: Comparison of research from the 1990s and 2000s ( opens in a new tab ) doi.org Why the command line feels scary System administrators said you cannot click your way around a command line to figure it out, and that it may be scary or overwhelming for a beginner; this is a survey quote, not a measured rate of mistakes 1 . Sources (1) Voronkov, Martucci and Lindskog, System Administrators Prefer Command Line Interfaces, Don't They? An Exploratory Study of Firewall Interfaces ( opens in a new tab ) arxiv.org Setup is the hard part Software Carpentry reports that installing software is often harder than using it, and that every new tool fails for at least one person in the room across Mac, Windows and Linux 1 . Sources (1) Wilson, Software Carpentry: lessons learned ( opens in a new tab ) doi.org Feedback builds confidence In a university Unix course with near-instant per-answer feedback, 78.2% of 2021 respondents said they had procedural Unix knowledge, against 38.8% before; the authors call this self-report possibly subjective, and the students were not solo first-timers 1 . Sources (1) Berry et al., ShellOnYou: learning by doing Unix command line ( opens in a new tab ) ctiber.github.io

Your terminal 0:00 – 0:09 Hook You have never opened a terminal. By the end of this page you will have run your first skill in one. 0:09 – 0:37 Why this page I split this into one step per screen, because a long setup guide feels like a wall and a single step feels like something you can finish. Every step hands you one thing that works and the next step needs it, so when you arrive at the workshop, we can start with a grilling session right away and nobody spends the first hour on setup.

Overview 0:00 – 0:24 Four pieces, one chain Here is the whole route in four pieces: a terminal, an AI agent, a folder and a skill. Each piece only works because the one before it works, so when the last one runs, you know the whole chain holds. It takes about twenty minutes, and you can stop after any step and come back. 0:24 – 0:42 Skip what you have If you already have an AI agent installed, jump straight to step five, because nothing before it changes for you. And if you would rather build the setup yourself than download it, the last Section is for you, so skip to the end.

Open your terminal 0:00 – 0:30 Not a personal failing If opening a terminal feels a little odd, that is a common reaction, and I would not read it as a sign that you are bad with computers. I think the fear comes from the blank window that gives you no hint what to press, and that is my hypothesis, not a proven fact. Nothing here asks you to prove anything, we only open the window and look at it. 0:30 – 0:52 One window, one cursor Pick your system in the toolbar, then find Terminal on a Mac, PowerShell on Windows, or the terminal on Linux, and open it. You will see a mostly empty window with a blinking cursor, and that is exactly what success looks like here. It is not frozen, it is waiting for you. 0:52 – 1:19 Stuck? Paste it If something looks different on your screen, you do not have to work it out alone. Paste your error into the troubleshooting box under the step, and it wraps your system, your AI agent and the step number into a prompt you can hand to a free ChatGPT. Every step below has one, so asking for help is part of the route.
Your AI agent 0:00 – 0:14 Terminal done So you now have a window that waits for words. Because an empty window cannot do much on its own, the next piece is the AI agent that will live inside it.

Your folder 0:00 – 0:17 Terminal and AI agent, now the place to work You have a terminal and an AI agent, so what is missing is a place to work. An AI agent works inside one folder and reads what is there, so we give it one on purpose: the starter folder.

Your first skill 0:00 – 0:17 Everything in place So everything is in place: a terminal, an AI agent and a folder. What is left is a skill, which is a small set of instructions your AI agent can follow, and running it shows that the chain is real.

The technical route 0:00 – 0:18 For people who build This last Section is for people who build, and it is optional. If you are comfortable with a terminal, you can get the same result without the starter folder by installing the pieces yourself. Everyone else can stop at the homepage.
